cards.title: Decoherence-free braided interaction

checks.reason: The main text states the braided zero-decay/nonzero-exchange result and the supplement derives it as Eq. gBraidedAtoms.
Substitution into the braided Table-I expressions cancels all decay terms and leaves g/gamma=1.
At phi=pi, the separate and nested zero-decay points instead have zero exchange, matching the paper's topology distinction.
The frozen grid contains pi/2 exactly and the target check records the expected four values.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate the frozen arrays at phi=pi/2 and compare against (g, Gamma_a, Gamma_b, Gamma_coll)=(1,0,0,0).

cards.title: General zero-decay factorization and topology implication

source_refs.value: Eqs. (S135)-(S137) and the discussion following Eq. (S137)

checks.reason: The emission-amplitude factorization is traced to Supplement Eqs. (S135)-(S137).
Expanding A_j A_k* reproduces the full cosine point-pair sum, so Gamma_j=0 implies every collective decay involving j is zero.
Separate and nested zero-phasor examples have zero exchange, while a braided example retains finite exchange.
Direct pair sums and the separately factorized phasor calculation agree for unequal rates and arbitrary connection counts.

cards.numerical_form: Evaluate arbitrary point/rate arrays by direct pair sums and independently by complex emission-amplitude factorization.

cards.title: Protected-chain constraint rank and independent couplings

checks.reason: The protected-chain phase constraints and coupling formulas are traced to Supplement Eqs. (S122)-(S128).
Selecting the even phase columns of C_N gives the N by N identity matrix for every N>=2, proving rank N without extrapolating a finite numerical rank.
The N-1 odd control phases are free and the even phases solve the N zero-decay equations exactly.
N=3,4,6 constructions have zero individual decay, no non-neighbor exchange, and full N-1 coupling-control rank.

cards.numerical_form: Construct C_N, expose its identity rank witness, solve dependent phases, and evaluate all pair coefficients.

cards.title: All-to-all constraint count and N=3 constructions

checks.reason: The all-to-all constraints and printed N=3 constructions are traced to Supplement Eqs. (S129)-(S134).
The first N columns of the sliding-window constraint matrix form a unit upper-triangular matrix, proving rank N for every N>=2.
The printed N=3 equal and signed phase choices satisfy zero decay and reproduce their stated coupling relations.
The rank witness and free-control count hold at N=3,4,6; the exact witness supplies the all-N step.

cards.numerical_form: Construct B_N, verify its unit upper-triangular minor, and evaluate the two printed three-atom phase assignments.
